newsitem.title: USA: Fingerhut labor pact negotiations begin.
newsitem.headline: Fingerhut labor pact negotiations begin.

text.p: Fingerhut Cos told Reuters Monday that negotiations on a new labor agreement covering workers at three distribution centers in Minnesota began last week.

Talks with the Union of Needletrades, Industrial and Textile Employees (UNITE) began Friday, Fingerhut and union officials said. The company said the pact will cover 1,700 employees in Minnesota. The union estimated that the contract will cover more than 2,000 workers.
The contract is scheduled to expire next February, said Fingerhut, a direct marketing company. The next bargaining session is scheduled for December 3, the UNITE said.

Meanwhile, the company is continuing negotiations on a new contract covering 700 workers at a distribution facility in Bristol, Tenn. The contract expired in February, and workers have been working without a labor agreement while negotiations continued over the summer, a Fingerhut spokeswoman said.
Issues on the table include job security, pay raises and improved working conditions, the union said.

Fingerhut recently informed the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that a systems error mistakenly suspended collection of 600,000 accounts, contributing to a higher delinquency rate. The company said it could be forced to make provisions for uncollectible accounts if the higher delinquency persists.
